title: CMV Retinitis: Clinical Mastery & Management Protocol
summary: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis remains the most common and sight-threatening opportunistic ocular infection in patients with advanced HIV/AIDS. This guide covers the pathophysiology, diagnostic criteria, and aggressive management strategies required to prevent permanent visual loss.

sections.title: Definition & Epidemiology
sections.content: CMV retinitis is a necrotizing retinitis caused by Human Herpesvirus 5 (HHV-5). Historically, it affected 30-40% of AIDS patients with CD4+ counts < 50 cells/µL. While HAART has drastically reduced incidence, it remains a critical diagnosis in patients with poor treatment adherence or undiagnosed immunocompromise.

rows: Dense white retinal infiltrates, 'pizza-pie' appearance, hemorrhages
Peripheral granular, fine white dots, minimal hemorrhage
Severe perivascular sheathing mimicking frost on vessels
Very rapid, associated with high viral load

sections.title: Red Flags: Sight-Threatening Indicators
content: Involvement of the posterior pole (macula/optic nerve head)
Retinal detachment (Rhegmatogenous) due to retinal necrosis
Decreased visual acuity (VA < 20/40)
Any signs of optic nerve edema or infarction
New onset 'floaters' in a high-risk patient

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Sequence
content: Step 1: Dilated indirect fundoscopy (gold standard).
Step 2: CBC with differential and CD4+ count.
Step 3: Aqueous humor sampling (PCR) if diagnosis is ambiguous.
Step 4: Systemic screening for CMV (PCR, shell vial culture).
Step 5: Regular monitoring via color fundus photography (ETDRS protocol).

sections.title: Treatment Protocol
content: Induction Therapy: IV Ganciclovir (5 mg/kg BID for 14-21 days) or IV Foscarnet (60 mg/kg TID).
Maintenance Therapy: Valganciclovir (900 mg daily).
Intravitreal Options: Ganciclovir (2 mg/0.05 mL) or Foscarnet (2.4 mg/0.1 mL) for sight-threatening lesions.
HAART Initiation: Crucial to restore immune function (wait 2-4 weeks post-induction to avoid Immune Recovery Uveitis - IRU).
Retinal Detachment: Surgical intervention via pars plana vitrectomy with silicone oil tamponade.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: CMV retinitis is NOT associated with significant anterior chamber inflammation; if the eye is 'quiet', think CMV.
Immune Recovery Uveitis (IRU) occurs when CD4 counts rise; it manifests as vitritis and cystoid macular edema.
Always perform a baseline and serial CD4 testing to monitor immune status.
Valganciclovir is associated with neutropenia; monitor absolute neutrophil count (ANC) weekly.
Once a retinal scar forms, it is permanent; the goal is to prevent progression to the macula.
